```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(ggplot2)
library(ggpattern)
library(xgboost)
library(lme4)
library(splines)

source("../HelperFunctions/FeatureEngineeringRegularGridCleaned.R")
options(scipen=999)

seed_num <- 123
set.seed(seed_num)
```

#### [3a] Set up Python environment and functions

I would suggest setting up your conda environment outside of R, and verify that you can run this okay:
* conda create -n xgb_smep python=3.11 -y
* conda activate xgb_smep
* conda install -c conda-forge numpy pandas scikit-learn xgboost hyperopt -y
* python -c "import numpy, pandas, sklearn, xgboost, hyperopt; print('ok')"

After that, run the followings. Make sure that you give R the correct conda env name.

```{r}
## Run at the top of every session, BEFORE any other Python use.
library(reticulate)
# use_condaenv("vae", 
#              conda = "Path_to_Conda_or_Miniconda/envs/",
#              required = TRUE)

# If you get an error that your conda environment cannot be found, try
# setting the Python interpreter to the python.exe in your conda environment:
# 
# use_python("Path_to_Conda_or_Miniconda/envs/vae/python.exe", required = TRUE)
#py_config() #Check to see if you are using the correct Python interpreter

# defines the Python functions in FeatureEngineeringRegularGridCleaned
setup_hyperopt_xgb()                    

```

## 1. Simulate data

```{r}
NNow    <- 500
TmaxNow <- 300
TminNow <- 250

dat <- simulate_burst_ou_mixed2(
  N    = NNow,
  Tmin = TminNow,
  Tmax = TmaxNow,
  seed = seed_num,
  Tend = 30
)

```

### [1a] Pooled person-time XGB, supplied hyperparameters

Before running anything, notice that I set n_trials0 (number of permutation importance trials) to 10 for faster running. In the manuscript, I set this to 100.

The code chunk below runs the pooled person-time XGBoost analysis with supplied hyperparameters. 

```{r}

n_trials0 = 10 #Number of permutation importance trials; 100 in manuscript. Set to 10 for faster run
isPlot = FALSE #Whether to generate plots

pooled <- run_pooled_xgb(
  dat       = dat,
  targets   = c("Y1", "Y2"),
  n_trials  = n_trials0, #number of random subject-level train/test splits or trials
  test_prop = 0.30, #proportion of held-out (test) subjects
  n_repeats = 10, #How many times each predictor gets shuffled within a trial
  nrounds   = 300, #Number of boosting rounds
  params    = list(
    max_depth        = 3,
    eta              = 0.05,
    subsample        = 0.80,
    colsample_bytree = 0.80
  ),
  tune = FALSE,
  seed = seed_num
)


if (isPlot){
pdf("A_PooledXGB.pdf")
plot_perm_compare(
  perm_summary = pooled$perm_summary,
  value_col    = "mean_importance_pct",
  outcome_col  = "target",
  plot_title   = "(A) Pooled XGB w/o Hyperopt",
  y_lab        = "Mean % increase in loss"
)
dev.off()
}
```

#### [1b] Pooled XGB with Hyperopt-tuned hyperparameters

```{r}
pooled_tuned <- run_pooled_xgb(
  dat        = dat,
  targets    = c("Y1", "Y2"),
  n_trials   = n_trials0,
  test_prop  = 0.30,
  valid_prop = 0.20,
  n_repeats  = 10,
  tune       = TRUE,
  max_evals  = 30,
  seed       = seed_num
)

check_xgb_run(pooled, label = "pooled")
check_xgb_run(pooled_tuned, label = "pooled tuned")

pooled_tuned$perm_summary
pooled_tuned$params #Hyperparameters
summarize_hyperopt_params(pooled_tuned$params, label = "pooled")

#Compare untuned pooled xgb results
pooled$perm_summary
pooled$params

if (isPlot){
pdf("B_PooledXGB.pdf")
plot_perm_compare(
  perm_summary = pooled_tuned$perm_summary,
  value_col    = "mean_importance_pct",
  outcome_col  = "target",
  plot_title   = "(B) Pooled XGB w/ Hyperopt",
  y_lab        = "Mean % increase in loss"
)
dev.off()
}
```

### [2a] Sequential slow -> fast decomposition, supplied hyperparameters

```{r}
fast <- run_fast_xgb(
  dat        = dat,
  outcomes   = c("Y1_resid_sd", "Y2_resid_sd", "resid_CCF_0"),
  n_trials   = n_trials0,
  test_prop  = 0.30,
  valid_prop = 0.20,
  n_repeats  = 10,
  tune       = FALSE,
  seed       = seed_num,
  grid_step = .05
)

check_xgb_run(fast, label = "fast untuned")

fast$perm_summary

if (isPlot){
pdf("A_FastXGB_noHyper.pdf")
plot_perm_compare(
  perm_summary = fast$perm_summary,
  value_col    = "median_importance_pct",
  y_lab        = "Median % relative increase in test loss",
  plot_title   = "(A) Between-person XGB w/o Hyperopt",
  x_lim = c(0,30)
)
dev.off()

pdf("C_FastXGB_noHyper.pdf")
plot_perm_compare(
  perm_summary = fast$perm_summary,
  value_col    = "prop_positive",
  y_lab              = "Proportion +ve permutation importance",
  plot_title         = "(C) Between-person XGB w/o Hyperopt"
)
dev.off()
}

#Keep feature order from untuned model
ord <- with(fast$perm_summary,
            names(sort(tapply(mean_importance, feature, max), decreasing = TRUE)))

```

#### [2b] Sequential XGB with Hyperopt

The slow models are reused, not re-fit.

```{r}
fast_tuned <- run_fast_xgb(
  slow_models = fast$slow_models,   # now safe to reuse
  fast_feat   = fast$fast_feat,
  outcomes    = c("Y1_resid_sd", "Y2_resid_sd", "resid_CCF_0"),
  n_trials    = n_trials0,
  test_prop   = 0.30,
  valid_prop  = 0.20,
  n_repeats   = 10,
  tune        = TRUE,
  tune_by     = "outcome",
  max_evals   = 30,
  seed        = seed_num,
  grid_step = .05
)

if (isPlot){
pdf("B_FastXGB_Hyper.pdf")
plot_perm_compare(
  perm_summary       = fast_tuned$perm_summary,
  value_col    = "median_importance_pct",
  y_lab        = "Median % relative increase in test loss",
  plot_title   = "(B) Between-person XGB w/ Hyperopt",
  feature_order = ord,
  x_lim = c(0,30)
)
dev.off()

pdf("D_FastXGB_Hyper.pdf")
plot_perm_compare(
  perm_summary       = fast_tuned$perm_summary,
  value_col    = "prop_positive",
  y_lab        = "Proportion +ve permutation importance",
  plot_title   = "(D) Between-person XGB w/ Hyperopt",
  feature_order = ord
)
dev.off()
}
```

### [2c] Compare tuned and untuned fast-XGB models

```{r}
check_xgb_run(fast, label = "fast untuned, per outcome")
check_xgb_run(fast_tuned, label = "fast tuned, per outcome")

# To get permutation importance summary measures
perm_sum <- fast_tuned$perm_summary
perm_sum[perm_sum$target=="resid_CCF_0" & (perm_sum$feature=="Y1_acf1"|
 perm_sum$feature=="Y2_acf1"|
 perm_sum$feature=="Y1_entropy"),]

perm_sum[(perm_sum$feature=="X2i"|
 perm_sum$feature=="X3i"|
 perm_sum$feature=="X4i"),]

# Inspect the hyperparameters used
t(sapply(fast_tuned$params_by_outcome, function(p)
  round(unlist(p[c("max_depth", "n_estimators", "learning_rate",
                   "min_child_weight", "subsample","colsample_bytree",
                   "reg_lambda")]), 4)))



```

### [3] Predicted curves from a saved model

```{r}
curve_y1 <- xgb_pred_curve(
  model      = pooled_tuned$models$Y1,
  x_var      = "time",
  by         = "I_b",
  n_grid     = 60,
  recompute  = function(d) { d$I_b_X3 <- d$I_b * d$X3_t; d },
  plot_title = "(C) Pooled XGB: predicted y1 over time"
)

if (isPlot){
pdf("C_PooledXGB.pdf")
print(curve_y1$plot)
dev.off()
}

# Pooled Y2 over time, split by burst indicator.
# recompute rebuilds the I_b * X3_t product column after I_b is varied.
curve_y2 <- xgb_pred_curve(
  model      = pooled_tuned$models$Y2,
  x_var      = "time",
  by         = "I_b",
  n_grid     = 60,
  recompute  = function(d) { d$I_b_X3 <- d$I_b * d$X3_t; d },
  plot_title = "(D) Pooled XGB: predicted y2 over time"
)

if (isPlot){
pdf("D_PooledXGB.pdf")
print(curve_y2$plot)
dev.off()
}

```
